title: This Hidden Glacier Has Enough Water to Fill 600 Olympic Swimming Pools - Nautilus
gist: Utah's rock-covered Timpanogos Glacier holds enough water to fill 600 Olympic pools, and a new gravity-based measurement technique is quantifying the ~51,000 hidden rock glaciers worldwide that serve as climate-resilient water reservoirs.

themes.theme: Rock glaciers as hidden water reserves

insights.claim: Rock glaciers are glaciers hidden beneath layers of loose rock tens to hundreds of feet thick, making them hard to see and measure.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Explains why a major water resource has gone largely unquantified.

insights.claim: By some estimates there are roughly 51,000 rock glaciers worldwide—836 in Utah alone—and they act as climate-resilient water reservoirs and vital alpine wildlife habitats.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Flags a globally significant, climate-resilient freshwater store relevant to water-security planning.
insights.locator: there are roughly 51,000 of these hidden glaciers

insights.claim: The Timpanogos Glacier alone holds enough water to fill roughly 600 Olympic swimming pools.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Quantifies the scale of water stored in a single hidden glacier.
insights.locator: Enough Water to Fill 600 Olympic Swimming Pools

insights.claim: Utah University-led geologists measured the Timpanogos Glacier by detecting tiny variations in gravitational acceleration between ice and rock at over 230 grid locations, correcting even for the positions of the sun and moon.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A novel technique that could unlock measurement of the world's many buried rock glaciers.
insights.locator: developed a novel technique that relied on detecting gravity
